# Review

## Summary

The body mostly defines its terms in place. The hypothetical agent grounds "revision workflow" and "revision capability". The note glosses "repeatable operative path" through the functions it keeps available: evidence, proposed change, adoption decision, installation and later use. "Non-regression requirement" is ordinary engineering vocabulary, and the note supplies its operative condition, the checked scope.

The one gap is the opening supplement line. It positions the note through two undefined KB-internal phrases. The rest of the note remains readable without that line, so the problem is a warning rather than a failure. Still, the first sentence a reader meets fails this gate's test.

# Review

## Summary

The title is a genuine claim, but as a modal possibility statement it is hard to argue against: an informed reader would readily grant that an improvement can disable later improvement. The note does establish something more contestable — that verifying the current gain says nothing about whether the revision mechanism survives, and that non-regression only protects it under a scope condition. Someone could reasonably argue the opposite of that (for example, that a non-regression requirement already implies preserved improvability). Sharpening the title toward that point would let it clear this gate cleanly.

# Review

## Summary

The note is short and its main parts do real work. The hypothetical agent makes the failure concrete. The non-regression section states the condition under which the failure is prevented. The section on remaining able to improve separates preservation from actual later improvement. The first Scope bullet, about fixed deployments that deliberately give up self-revision, adds a boundary the body does not otherwise state.

The redundancy is local. Three chunks restate a point that an adjacent or earlier passage has already made. The first is the "no contradiction" paragraph after the example. The second is the "therefore ... only under an additional condition" sentence, which repeats the scope rule it follows. The third is the Scope bullet about another applicable path, which the body already covers. Cutting or folding these would shorten the note without removing anything the reader needs.

The sentence "That note supplies the detailed test; this note explains why a successful improvement comparison can miss its failure" was considered and is not flagged. It tells the reader where the detailed test lives, which the earlier link alone does not.

# Review

The note is mostly literal. The title's "close the path" and the repeated "revision path" work as precise shorthand: the body defines a path as the route from evidence to proposal, adoption, installation and later use, and the linked repeatable-operative-path note uses the same term. That figure is kept.

One heading uses a figure whose connotation the note does not support. "Consume" suggests that the faster configuration gains its speed by using up the revision workflow. The example never says that the speed comes from removing the workflow, and the following paragraph explicitly separates the measured gain from the removed capability. The literal verb "disable" states the intended relation just as clearly and does not suggest that the two effects are coupled.

# Review

Most load-bearing assertions are exact.

- **The worked example.** It names the workflow, the change and the lost route.
- **The replacement condition.** It requires a replacement to "carry another revision through to use".
- **The Scope entries.** They state the system boundary and alternative paths.

The note's operative recommendation is the sentence that says what non-regression must check. That sentence leaves the object of the checked capability unresolved between producing another revision and revising the improvement machinery. The two readings call for different checks in a declared comparison, so the difference is material.

# Review

## Summary

Most mechanism statements are framed at the right level. Non-regression protects whatever is in its checked scope. The example's comparison checked task performance while the change removed a different capability. Preservation attaches to the function, not to a component.

The opening paragraph is the exception. It names only selection and installation as the disabled functions. Later, the note defines the relevant question as the full chain from evidence to later use. Its replacement criterion is whether a revision can be carried "through to use". A reader of the opening alone would miss losses at the proposal or later-use stages. The later text corrects this, so the narrowing is local, but it does exclude covered cases.

# Review

## Summary

The note's negations scope cleanly. Examples are "does not check that the revision mechanism survives", "only under an additional condition" and "is not improving again". Its "when" and "if" clauses attach to the intended verbs. Most pronouns have clear antecedents. "Their changes" refers to the old files. "Its preservation" in the Scope bullet refers to self-revision.

One pronoun is a plausible misreading. In the files-remain-editable paragraph, "its failure" most naturally attaches to the adjacent "successful improvement comparison", not to the revision path it is meant to name.

# Friction check: An improvement can close the path to further improvement

**Central claim (one sentence):** A successor can improve declared production performance while disabling the system's route for selecting and installing later revisions, and non-regression prevents this only when that revision capability is in the checked scope.

## Filter
**Filter:** SURVIVES

The claim commits to two properties that coexist: a real production gain and a real loss of revision capability. Nothing in the gain requires keeping the capability, and nothing in the loss requires giving up the gain. The conditional remedy, scoping non-regression to the capability, does not contradict either property. The Scope section consistently bounds the claim to declared system boundaries and to the absence of another applicable path.

## Thinnest joints

The two thinnest joints come at the main transitions. The first is the move from the example to the section heading's causal language. The second is the move from the example to the non-regression remedy, where the capability placed in scope differs from the capability the example lost. The third joint is the remedy's implied sufficiency: scoping the capability is treated as if it ensured detection, but the check's means of exercising a dispositional capability is never stated. The two `HOLDS` joints are the note's local inferences about disjoint capabilities. They hold under the example as stated and rank last.

## For the human
Look first at whether the checked-scope sentence should name the first-order capability the example loses, and whether "prevents" should be conditioned on a check that exercises the revision path.

# Critique: An improvement can close the path to further improvement

**Note:** kb/theory/an-improvement-can-close-the-path-to-further-improvement.md
**Central commitment:** A successor can improve a declared production dimension while disabling the machinery that would produce another revision, and non-regression prevents this only when revision capability is included in the checked scope.
**Critique mode:** claim
**Attack outcome:** partially lands

## Strongest case against it

The opponent is an engineer who designs self-modifying agent loops, for example an archive-and-evaluate loop. In such a loop, a modified agent enters the archive only after a check confirms it can still edit code. The opponent accepts the first half of the note: a production gain and a lost revision path are compatible. That point is close to the general rule that a check covers only what it measures, and the note states it correctly. The objection targets the second half. The note says non-regression "protects" the revision path, and that preservation is "a consequence of non-regression", once revision capability is in the checked scope. The opponent says scope inclusion is necessary but not sufficient. Two further conditions do the protective work.

1. **The check must control adoption.** In the better-factory framework this note supplements, non-regression is part of a comparison that judges the *installed* successor. The parent note says this directly: "A comparison judges the adopted states. Whether an evaluator also controlled adoption is a separate causal question." A correctly scoped comparison that runs after installation reports that the successor fails, but by then the path is already closed. This loss differs from a production regression. A regressed production capability can be repaired by a later revision. A closed revision path removes the internal route that would make the repair. For the agent at the declared boundary, a failed verdict that arrives after installation cannot be acted on. This is the note's own hypothetical: the faster configuration has been installed and has removed the workflow.

2. **Revision capability must be checkable before installation.** Production non-regression can be checked by running the task set on the candidate. Revision capability has no equivalent check that is just as simple. The linked repeatable-path note accepts two kinds of evidence for continuity: a later episode, which comes after installation, and a specified transition mechanism that survives the transition. Only the second kind, or a trial revision run in staging, is available when the adoption decision is made. "Include it in the checked scope" therefore points to a check whose feasible form the note leaves unstated.

On this view, the note puts the protective mechanism in scope declaration. The work is actually done by a gate that runs before installation, using evidence that is available before installation. Getting scope right without that gate yields an accurate post-mortem, not protection.

## How the note engages it

Partially engaged. The body sentence about a successor that destroys the only applicable revision path is accurate: it says the successor "fails the requirement", not that it is prevented. The note also hands the detailed operational test to the repeatable-path note ("That note supplies the detailed test"). The separation between judging states and controlling adoption appears only in the parent note's Scope. This note's description ("non-regression prevents this"), section heading ("When non-regression protects the revision path") and conclusion ("a consequence of non-regression") each turn the necessary scope condition into protection without stating the adoption condition. The timing of the check is not discussed. The third section ("Remaining able to improve is not improving again") answers a different objection, about over-reading preservation, not the objection that preservation is under-delivered.

## Constructive findings

- State that scope inclusion makes a path-closing successor *fail* non-regression, and that this *prevents* closure only when the check gates installation. Otherwise the check records the loss after installation. One sentence in "When non-regression protects the revision path" would do it. The description's "prevents" should then match.
- Name the pre-installation form of the check: a trial revision carried through representation, determination, admission and installation in staging, or an argument from a specified transition mechanism. This also explains why non-regression on ordinary production tasks cannot cover revision capability: the task set never exercises the revision path.
- Optionally, add to Scope that the path closes for good at the declared boundary when the successor removes the only revision path. This is the asymmetry with ordinary regressions that makes adoption-time checking matter more here.

## Secondary objections (optional)

- The note names no safeguard other than non-regression. Keeping the revision machinery outside the edit surface the successor can change protects the path without any check. The note's literal claim is limited to non-regression, so this does not refute it. A contrast would still stop readers from treating scope inclusion as the only remedy.
- The opening argument ("Checking the current gain does not check that the revision mechanism survives") is close to the general rule that a check covers only what it measures. The note's specific contribution is the claim that production task sets do not exercise the revision path. That claim is implied, not stated, and stating it would make the note's reach clearer.

# Premise decomposition: An improvement can close the path to further improvement

**Register:** claim
**Central commitment (one sentence):** A successor can improve a declared production dimension while disabling the machinery that would produce another revision, and non-regression prevents this only when the revision capability is included in the checked scope.

## Premises and counterexamples

The commitment has two parts. The first is a possibility claim. It consumes the premise that production gain and revision capability can separate, and the premise that a production check does not see the revision mechanism. The second is a conditional about non-regression. It consumes the premise that a requirement protects only what it checks. In the section's sufficiency reading, it also consumes the premise that including revision capability in the checked scope is enough to catch its loss. Two background premises let "loss of revision capability" be judged: the capability is identified by its function rather than its component, and loss is relative to a declared system boundary.

The possibility half survives: one coherent hypothetical establishes "can". Both dents fall on the non-regression half and are local. The general sentence that a production check never sees the revision mechanism needs the decoupling condition that the hypothetical quietly supplies. The sufficiency phrasing in "When non-regression protects the revision path" exceeds what the description commits to, because a checked scope can include the capability and still miss a latent break. Each dent can be repaired with a qualification in `## Scope` without changing the claim. No premise failed globally.

## For the human

Look first at "Checking the current gain does not check that the revision mechanism survives". It is stated universally, and it fails when production performance depends on the revision mechanism. Add the decoupling condition, or say that coupled revision counts as being within the checked scope.

# Simplification synthesis: An improvement can close the path to further improvement
